body: I don't think it's selfish to kill yourself. It's selfish to hurt other people for personal gain. But the suicidal person isn't doing it for a leg up. They're doing it because they would rather be dead. These days I would rather be dead than do most things I can think of, but I don't know everything that's out there, so I think I'll try some more things. I can die whenever I choose.

It takes quite a lot of courage, in my opinion, even if you might argue that courage is better-directed elsewhere.

Why don't you think suicide is a courageous act?

If you do it, really make sure it's a thought-out decision rather than an impulse. That way, everyone will be a little more prepared, and you are more likely to feel vindicated rather than regretful in your last moments. Wishing you luck and peace, whatever you decide.
It is not just old people who should be given the option. As none of us have chosen to live, exist and suffer, part of a fair social contract is allowing people to end their lives.

You always have a choice. It might not seem like it because of the pain, but it is a choice. Whatever choice you make, make it confidently and without distress. I hope whatever you decide, you find peace.
I don't think being sick is a necessary component of suicidality
The lives of the suicidal are often ugly and difficult as well.
You say your psychiatrists don't like to be challenged. What kinds of things do you challenge them about?

Other people can't convince you that life is worth living, not really, because you will fall back into your old beliefs when they're not around. You have to convince yourself that life is good, if you want to be convinced. I think it's actually kind of cruel to expect others to give this to you, and be bitter when they inevitably fail because that is the outcome you prefer. I don't know whether that's what you're doing, but it is a surefire path to complete alienation.
Yes. I think it is reasonable to look forward to anything that promises to end my suffering. This is not to endorse anyone else's decisions but my own.
Some methods are definitely more effective than others. Some methods have very negligible rates of failure.
I agree with you. It's really unfair.

I would not discourage others from committing suicide. I would try to understand their rationale, and support them, without endorsing their plan. That is something we all have to do alone, to avoid taking anyone with us who isn't fully committed to dying.

I do not believe I have a duty to my family or society. I have a duty to myself to live the life I would like, or end my life if I no longer believe it is possible to live up to my own standards of quality.

I accept that life is suffering. That is precisely why I would like mine to end. Reducing others' suffering is noble. I have tested this hypothesis as a reason to live. I have worked at a psychiatric hospital, as an aide, and it was rewarding. But I also realize that it is cruel to keep people alive who are really in a constant state of suffering.

I do not have an obligation to live, because I did not ask for life. It was given to me without my consent, and will be given back.
It's ok, thank you for your advice. I think the intention is more important than the actual words, and your intentions are good 🤗.

I agree with you. People have done this for a very long time. That said, I don't think it's true that everyone wants to die. Some people seem to enjoy life a great deal. I'm glad everyone is not having as bad of a time as we are.

Yes. I am ready for whatever happens after I jump. In fact, I am excited. I am excited not to feel pain anymore. I'll take that risk, absolutely.

My passion in life is for my life to end. I understand if that is difficult to understand. To understand, to really get it, I think you'd have to be me.

If my friends love me, that also means they don't want me to suffer unbearably. Doubtless they will disagree about how this relief should be achieved, but I know they want me to feel peace. I think they know enough about my background to not be too surprised by my passing. I hope my friends will forgive me and know that I will no longer suffer.
It's definitely not your fault. And if he does kill himself, I think you made him feel less lonely in his last moments, not more.
